name: Mora

anatomy.part: beak tip of the ptarmigan's head, pointing right
head, at the eye (centre of the round head)
nape where the neck dips into the back

myth: Mora was a ptarmigan who could not make up her mind. In summer she wore brown like cliff moss; in winter she went white as drift, and was proud of both. Aun watched her change in one week and laughed until he dropped his string. Hesk heard the laughing and said nothing, which is her way. She wound Mora up into the north and hung her there, head high, where every house could see. Tavo the Gale came down the Reach and tried to shake her loose, but she held. Ennu the Kite-Wright says a sensible person changes coat when the weather asks, not when the neighbours do. Old women still say it over the nets, and young men who swap opinions every morning are called Mora's cousins. The bird does not mind. She has been brown and white a thousand times, and no one has talked her out of either.
verse:
Brown all summer long,
white as snow when winter comes—
Mora laughs at us.
